adr_serious_criteria: Per ADR, "serious criminal cases" are: offences for which the maximum punishment is of five years or more; non-bailable offences; electoral offences (e.g. IPC Section 171E or bribery); offences related to losses to the exchequer; assault, murder, kidnap, or rape-related offences; those mentioned in Representation of the People Act (Section 8); offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act; and crimes against women.
severity_method: Serious/non-serious applied from ADR's published 'serious criminal cases' criteria (5+ years max punishment; electoral offences; corruption/loss to exchequer; heinous categories incl. murder/attempt/rape/kidnap; SC/ST POA Act; crimes against women) to the IPC/statute sections listed in each affidavit. myneta.info does not publish ADR's own per-candidate split, so this is a transparent mechanical application, not ADR's official label. Borderline calls are noted per charge. All cases are declared/pending unless stated convicted; none of this implies guilt.
